$comment: GH-546 (stage 0) — THE DECLARED FORM OF AN ANALYSIS RESULT.
Why this file exists. Until now the form of the analysis result was whatever the
browser happened to hold at the moment it posted: the producer emitted a key only
when its value was not undefined, the server checked 'is it an array', and the
consumers each guarded with ?? null. A row of 5 keys and a row of 14 were equally
valid to everyone except a person reading the database. This file is the one place
that says what a complete result IS, and it is read by the producer when it builds
the body and by the server when it validates one.
Where the numbers come from — three sources, and they agree.
1. The producer, read from source: collectDashboardMetrics() in
assets/hub-persistence.js can emit 17 keys, listed under producer.emits with
the branch that emits each.
2. The rows on the stand, read 22.09 (SELECT only): 11 rows carry the 13 core
keys, one of those 11 carries companionDisease as a 14th, one carries 12 (no
weatherSource), and one carries 5.
3. The consumers, read from source — see divergence below.
What this file does NOT do yet. Nothing reads it at runtime: the producer still
assembles by presence and the server still validates 'is it an array'. Stage 1
gives the server a service that validates against this; stage 2 gives the producer
a body built from it. Stage 0 is the declaration and the test that it matches the
tree — a schema nobody checks is a comment.
Live tests were banned for this work and the stand was not touched: no run was
performed to snapshot the form. The producer enumeration is static, and the stand
rows are corroboration read with SELECT, not a measurement of a run.
required: a completed run must carry every one of these. A run that could not
produce a value sends the key with null and the outcome says why — 'twelve keys'
must become impossible to express, which is what Russley's row is today.
The 13 below are exactly the intersection of the eleven full rows on the stand.
Emitted only when the named condition holds. Present in the schema so that a
row carrying one is not 'an unknown key', and a row lacking one is not
'incomplete'.
conditional.companionDisease: the site has a companion surface — GAIP_COMPANION_DISEASE_RESULT._companionSurface; on the stand: Test6 - UK only
conditional.vwc: a sensor reading was available at the run; on the stand: no row carries it

$comment: THE FINDING OF THIS STAGE, and it contradicts one line of the plan.
collectDashboardMetrics() has two mutually exclusive climate branches:
if (_cm)       — global.climateMetrics — emits growthPotential, gdd, et, soilTemp
else if (_cc)  — orchestrator computed.climate — emits growthPotential, soilTemp
So gdd and et ARE emitted by today's producer, on the _cm branch. The plan's
section 4 says 'no run today emits them'; its section 1 says the opposite and is
right — Federal Golf's five-key row carries et and gdd and is the _cm branch.
What the stand shows and what it means: all eleven full rows went through _cc
(none carries gdd or et), and the one _cm row is the thinnest on the stand. The
branch is therefore not chosen by whether the run completed, and a body built
from this schema must decide which branch is the contract rather than inherit
whichever fired. That decision belongs to stage 2, not here; the keys are
declared so that the choice is visible instead of silent.
branchDependent.gdd: emitted only by the _cm branch (global.climateMetrics present)
branchDependent.et: emitted only by the _cm branch (global.climateMetrics present)

$comment: The top-level keys of the computed subtree. Unlike metrics these are not
enumerated by a single producer function — `computed` is the orchestrator's state
subtree copied wholesale — so this list is the CONSUMER side: the top-level keys
that files reading GAIP_DASHBOARD_DATA actually read.
Declared as observed, not as required: stage 0 does not decide which of these a
completed run must carry, because no single function produces them. Stage 1's
service validates metrics against `required` above; computed is validated only as
'an object'. Named here so the next stage has a list to work from rather than a
grep.
$comment2: GH-641 (link 11, analyst section 4.13в) — WHICH STEPS A CONSUMER KEY IS
ASSEMBLED FROM, for the keys the row's PRODUCER builds rather than a pass
The composer of an empty section's sentence has to find the cause recorded
against the step behind a key. For a key an engine writes, the dependency
graph already says which engine that is. These do not appear there, because
the pass does not write them: the producer assembles them afterwards out of
other steps' results. Declaring them as a graph node's output would be a lie
about the pass, and the guard for 'declared but not produced' would say so.
So they are declared HERE, beside the key, in the same file the server
already reads. An empty list is a statement too: no step stands behind the
key, so 'the cause was not recorded' is the truth about it rather than a gap
MEASURED, not assumed: `applicationWindow` appears in none of the 66 stored
rows, neither at the top level nor inside `disease` — nothing produces it,
and the disease page reads it as a fallback. `soilTempPhysics` is computed
while the panel is drawn, which is its own open item.
$comment3: GH-667 (queue item 3ag) — WHEN A SECTION IS EMPTY THOUGH ITS OBJECT IS NOT.
`soilNutrition` is never an empty object: the producer fills it with a shape
— verdict, depths, ten nutrient cards — even when nothing was measured. So
the general predicate, which asks whether the object has anything in it,
answers 'produced' while the screen shows NO DATA and ten dashes. Measured on
row 70 of `Test6 - UK`, a site with no soil sample at all: 17 keys,
`nutrients` of length TEN, every `actual` a dash, `pH`/`CEC`/`ECe`/`soilNa`
THE MARKER IS DECLARED HERE, AND IT IS DECLARED THE SAME WAY FOR ANY SECTION.
The analyst's decision (her 4.13e/4.13zh): a section is empty when the
producer's own verdict says so. This is not a rule about soil inside the
composer, and it is not a count of readings — `nutrients` has ten entries in
both the empty and the filled row, so counting the cards distinguishes
nothing. `NO DATA` is written exactly when nothing was measured (GH-576).
A section with no entry here keeps the general predicate unchanged.

$comment: GH-557 (section 15) — THE ENVELOPE A RESULT TRAVELS IN, and what its
outcome means.
There were two outcomes and `complete` meant 'the POST was accepted'. With
GH-553 the producer sends every required key, null where its engine could
not answer, and the server accepts null as a complete value - so a run that
computed six of thirteen numbers was stored as a completed analysis and
replaced the numbers of one that had computed all thirteen.
`complete` now means ALL REQUIRED VALUES WERE COMPUTED. A run that finished
but could not compute some of them is `partial`. The server decides which,
from the body - the client's word is not the outcome.

outcomeRule.complete: every required metric has a value, and the run reported no skipped step
outcomeRule.partial: the run finished and the body passed the form, but a required metric is null or a step was skipped
outcomeRule.failed: no result was produced; `reason` says why

detail.$comment: Carried by the producer, stored with the row, returned by the projection and printed by the panel.
detail.nulls: required metrics the run could not compute
detail.skipped: [{step, module, reason}] - steps that did not run, from the orchestrator's own account
detail.notApplicable: [{module, missing}] - GH-777 (queue item 4, slice 2): modules this SITE is not a case for, which is a third answer beside a value and a gap. `missing` names the inputs of the calculation list whose absence makes the module inapplicable, and is EMPTY when the engine itself ran and answered `not here` - dew is that case. The server judges each named input against the set recorded when the run started (GH-675), so the client is told either `you have not entered it` or `it was there and did not reach us`, and never the wrong one of the two. An entry here does NOT make a run partial: a site without irrigation water is not an incomplete analysis.
detail.warnings: [{module, message, at, data}] - everything the pass said while running
detail.assumptions: [{key, displayName, providedValue, assumedValue, impact, confidencePenalty, affectedEngines, settingsField, settingsLabel, reason}] - GH-581: what the run PUT IN PLACE of something it was not given. Not the same as `skipped`: an assumption is a run that went ahead on a stand-in, a skip is a part that did not run at all, and the reader needs that difference. Taken from `GilbaIdentityEnforcement.getIdentityState().assumptions`, not re-derived.

inputs.$comment: GH-581 (stage 2) - WHAT THE RUN WAS GIVEN. The column has existed since GH-550 and was written null on every row, because nothing sent it. Two runs - one on live weather, one on a week-old cache; one on a site with a rootzone profile, one where the profile was filled in - were indistinguishable in the stored result. Identities and states only: the numbers are already in `metrics` and `computed`, and a second copy of them here would be a second source. Absent as a whole (null) means the record could not be assembled, which is a fact about the run, not a default.
inputs.weather: {status, source, readyAt} - what the weather was and when it arrived
inputs.normals: {present, source} - whether monthly climate normals were there
inputs.samples: {soil, water, tissue} - the id of the active sample of each type, or null
inputs.sensors: {vwc, soilTemp} - which of them answered, or null

$comment: Producer against consumers — the list stage 0 owes the owner. NO FIXES IN THIS
PASS: this is the perimeter, and each line is for a decision, not for a change.
HOW IT WAS MEASURED, AND THE LIMIT OF IT. The producer side is exact: every key
collectDashboardMetrics() can assign, read from source. The consumer side is NOT
exact and cannot be made so by grep: consumers alias the object first
(`var metrics = dbData.metrics`) and then pass it into functions, so a search for
`metrics.<key>` finds reads of any object called metrics and misses reads through
a differently named local. Both errors are real: a wide search returns 23 names
including `push`, `length` and `js`; a narrow one returns 5. The list below is
therefore what can be said with certainty from the three sources, and the
uncertain part is named rather than rounded off.

producerEmitsNoStandRowCarries.$comment: Emitted by the producer, absent from all 12 rows on the stand.
producerEmitsNoStandRowCarries.why: needs a sensor reading at the moment of the run; no site on the stand had one

$comment: Present ONLY on Federal Golf's 5-key row and on no complete row. This is the
pair that made the thin row look like 'a different collector' until the plan
traced it to the _cm branch.

carriedByOneRowOnly.why: conditional on a companion surface; Test6 - UK
